description: Aero L-29 Delfin listed in the Damascus Military Museum collection. The whole Damascus Military Museum inventory used here comes from aviationmuseum.eu, whose Syria pages date from 2015 to 2016, and no post-war confirmation was obtained. Esri imagery of 31 May 2025 shows the Tekkiye and Madrasa Sulaymaniyah courtyards standing and apparently undamaged but no aircraft could be resolved outdoors, so these airframes may be indoors, may have been moved, or may be gone. Existed around 2015; current state unknown.

Campbell Cricket single-seat autogyro carrying the British civil registration G-AXVL, listed in the Damascus Military Museum collection and by some margin the oddest item in it. Same currency caveat as the rest of this museum: the source is aviationmuseum.eu circa 2015-16 and Esri imagery of 31 May 2025 resolves no aircraft in the museum courtyards. Existed around 2015; current state unknown.

Remains of an Israeli Air Force Dassault Mirage IIIBJ two-seater listed in the Damascus Military Museum as a war trophy. Recorded as a wreck, but a shot-down enemy aircraft deliberately retained and put on public exhibition is a museum exhibit rather than battlefield debris, so it is included. Source is aviationmuseum.eu circa 2015-16; no post-war confirmation obtained.

Remains of an Israeli Air Force McDonnell Douglas F-4E Phantom II listed in the Damascus Military Museum as a war trophy. Recorded as a wreck but deliberately retained and publicly exhibited, so included as a museum exhibit. Source is aviationmuseum.eu circa 2015-16; no post-war confirmation obtained. Do not confuse this airframe with the separate Phantom remains at the October War Panorama on the other side of Damascus.
